split_rationale: E2 asks for a descriptive first-24-hour peak-lactate association. The former lactate trajectory card required serial measurements, clearance, landmarking, and trajectory stability, so generic lactate aliases were removed and a peak-specific card was created.

evidence_groups.claim_group: locked early peak lactate and mortality association
evidence_groups.pre_review_conclusion: Directly supports an observational association, not a causal effect.
The current adult guideline supports measuring and serially assessing lactate in the appropriate sepsis context; it does not turn this descriptive ICU-wide association into a treatment effect.
Supports auditing measured versus unmeasured patients without prescribing one universal correction model.
Prospective claims require landmark or time-varying handling; descriptive same-admission associations must disclose overlap.
Supports reporting cohort, variables, missing data, and analysis methods, not disease-specific choices.

required_signoff: The target is a descriptive association, not a treatment effect or deployable prediction.
Time zero is ICU admission and the primary exposure window is ICU hours 0-24.
Values after death or discharge are excluded from the peak.

The primary association population has at least one valid typed 0-24-hour lactate; the full eligible cohort remains the measured-versus-unmeasured audit denominator and unmeasured lactate is never zero-coded.
Specimen, assay, and unit harmonization are available from the typed data contract.
The primary model reports uncertainty and assesses nonlinearity.
Adjustment variables have prespecified baseline roles rather than being every available column.
Early death, early discharge, time under observation, and measurement intensity are reported as exposure-opportunity audits for the declared estimand.
